name: Light Fluorite Green
lede: Light Fluorite Green is a pale, yellow-leaning green named for fluorite, the mineral whose green variety can glow under ultraviolet light.

sections.title: Named for a glowing mineral
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 atlas gives this swatch at plate XXXII, hue 33″, tone d, and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system files it in block 119, a light yellow green [1]. In Munsell terms it reads 4.6GY 8.2/3.1 [1]. Fluorite is best known for the fluorescence that gave the phenomenon its name; the mineral's green variety is one of its more common colors, though this pale a tint has no separate record in Maerz and Paul's dictionary [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[oural-green]], [[pale-turtle-green]] and [[pale-veronese-green]], at 4.5, 
It sits between [[sage]] and [[celadon]] in tone, paler and more yellow than either [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this pale green in 166 of 23,781 paintings, about seven tenths of one per cent [2]. The earliest match is a 1413 landscape by the Japanese ink painter Oguri Sotan, five centuries before Ridgway's plate, so that is a lookalike hue and not a pigment record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The 1800s show the strongest lift, at nearly double the overall baseline rate [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings and ink works, and a match is not a test for fluorite or any other mineral [2].
